headline: Laughing off the broken arm

tr_quotes.text: It was very good of you and your wife to write even before you heard from me. You needn't feel in the least melancholy about me. I viewed the affair from the first as mainly comic in character. Now I can dress myself all right, and do about everything but ride and row; all I minded missing was the rest of the hunting season. . . Every now and then I like to drink the wine of life with brandy in it.

headline: A harsh lecture on the West
summary: Lecturing in New York City about the West, Roosevelt makes sweeping, disparaging remarks about American Indians, ranking even a vicious cowboy above them in moral character. The words reflect prejudices common among white Americans of his day and are recorded here as he spoke them.

tr_quotes.text: I don't go so far as to think that the only good Indians are the dead Indians but I believe nine out of every ten are and I shouldn't like to inquire too closely into the case of the tenth. The most vicious cowboy has more moral principle than the average Indian.

uncertain: The entry opens with a stray fragment ('to be carried on every U.S. ship') that seems to belong to another date; it was ignored.
